relations.assertion: Knocking down p53 triggers apoptosis and autophagy and inhibits migration in SSC-4 cells.
relations.evidence: Knocking down of p53 triggers apoptosis and autophagy, concomitantly with inhibition of migration on SSC-4 oral squamous carcinoma cells.
relations.surface_form: triggers apoptosis and autophagy, concomitantly with inhibition of migration

relations.assertion: SSC-4 cells are oral squamous carcinoma cells.
Oral squamous cell carcinoma is a malignancy.
relations.evidence: Oral squamous cell carcinoma (OSCC) is a malignancy

relations.assertion: p53 has a crucial role in proliferation and apoptosis during the occurrence and development of numerous malignant tumors.
relations.evidence: p53 has a crucial role in proliferation and apoptosis during the occurrence and development of numerous malignant tumors.

relations.assertion: Inhibiting p53 expression decreased proliferation ability, induced apoptosis/autophagy, and decreased migration in SSC-4 cells.
relations.evidence: We observed that inhibiting the expression of p53 decreased the proliferation ability and induced apoptosis/autophagy in SSC-4 cells. Moreover, we observed that this has decreased migration
relations.surface_form: decreased the proliferation ability and induced apoptosis/autophagy

relations.assertion: Inhibiting p53 expression blocked VEGF expression.
relations.evidence: We observed that inhibiting the expression of p53 decreased the proliferation ability and induced apoptosis/autophagy in SSC-4 cells. Moreover, we observed that this has decreased migration and has blocked the expression of VEGF.
relations.surface_form: has blocked the expression of VEGF

relations.assertion: A direct connection between p53 knockdown and OSCC cell death can be established.
relations.evidence: In conclusion, our research provides a proof that a direct connection between p53 knockdown and OSCC cell death can be established
relations.surface_form: a direct connection between p53 knockdown and OSCC cell death
